learning_outcomes.text: Be able to obtain confidence intervals for parameters of a normal population and to formulate and solve problems of statistical hypothesis testing, both parametric and non-parametric, in one or two populations.
Be able to synthesize and descriptively analyze a set of data.

Be able to formulate and solve simple and realistic linear programming problems. Synthesize the received information, formulate the relevant linear models, apply the Simplex method, and analyze and interpret the obtained solutions.
Be able to formalize and solve basic experimental design models.

Know how to calculate event probabilities from the definition and from the most common probability distributions, as well as from the probabilities of other events, using the properties of probability and conditional probabilities.

syllabus_topics: Hypothesis tests in one and two populations
teaching_methods: Self-study with recommended bibliography and software
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain at least 43% of the maximum score in each assessment component (continuous assessment and final exam) and a final weighted score of 5 or higher. If the minimum score is not reached in any part, the final grade will be the corresponding weighted average, with a maximum of 4.5 out of 10. Continuous assessment (30%) requires a minimum of 4.3/10 and is recoverable via a paper-based exam on the final exam day if not passed. The final written exam (70%) requires a minimum of 4.3/10. Passed parts from the first convocation are saved for the second convocation but not for subsequent academic years. For the extraordinary end-of-studies convocation, a single final written exam covering theory and problems will count for 100%.
